X.note: Warm, strong sunlight and a convincing weathered facade, but the figures are stiff, faceless mannequins scattered in a loose crowd. The left wall has a blown-out yellow patch and is mostly flat. The harbour view and the flag are nice.

Y.note: More varied wall materials, with stone courses, a base plinth and a green-shuttered window. The plaza has a hazier depth. The figures are still olive-grey mannequins, now bunched into a clump on the right. Some are hard to read against the sunlit cobbles. The empty beige plaza behind them looks washed out.

why: Both frames share the same toy-like mannequin crowd, but Y's richer facade detail and stronger atmospheric depth make it slightly more convincing as a place.
top_fix_for_weaker: Replace the identical grey-green mannequins in X with varied, properly clothed 1943 figures (khaki battledress, white naval uniforms, civilians), scaled to the street. Add the missing facade stonework courses and plinth, tone down the blown-out yellow patch on the left wall, and break up the loose crowd into purposeful groups.
anachronisms_seen: Generic faceless mannequin figures with no period-specific clothing detail
Pristine modern-looking blue-grey kiosk or box at the right of the plaza
Ship at the harbour is too indistinct to be period-verifiable
